transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've been really struggling because I keep hearing voices that other people can't hear. I also have this constant feeling that I'm being watched and monitored, and it's been going on like this for about six months now.

During these past six months, have you experienced any periods where your mood was exceptionally high, energetic, or irritable, or conversely, periods where you felt severely depressed, hopeless, or lacked all motivation?

No, I've never had any periods where I felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable. But for about the last month, I've been feeling deeply depressed, hopeless, and completely lacking any motivation or interest in doing anything.
Did the voices and the feeling of being watched start before you began feeling depressed, or did they only begin after your mood started to drop?

Yes, they started long before I began feeling depressed. The voices and the feeling of being watched have been going on for about six months now, whereas this deep depression only started about a month ago.
Are the voices and the feeling of being watched present every single day, or do they only happen when you are feeling depressed?

They don't only happen when I'm depressed. While they do happen at the same time now, there have definitely been times—like for a couple of weeks before this depression hit—where I heard the voices and felt watched even when my mood was completely fine.
Over the past six months, what is the total amount of time you have spent feeling depressed compared to the time you have felt like your mood was normal?

I would say I have been feeling depressed for the majority of the time over these past six months. There were only a few weeks where my mood felt somewhat normal, but otherwise, I've been feeling really down.
During the months when your mood was normal, were the voices and the feeling of being watched constant, or were there significant periods where you felt completely free of these experiences?
No, I didn't get any break from them at all. Even during those weeks when my mood felt normal, the voices and the feeling of being watched were constant and never went away.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports that the auditory hallucinations and delusions have been present for six months, while the depressive symptoms have only been present for one month. Furthermore, the patient experienced these psychotic symptoms for several weeks in the absence of any mood symptoms. Because the psychotic symptoms occurred independently of the mood episode and the mood symptoms have not been present for the majority of the total duration of the illness, the criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder are not met, and Schizophrenia is now the primary candidate.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has experienced persistent auditory hallucinations and delusions (being watched) for six months. These psychotic symptoms were present for a significant period (five months) in the absence of a major mood episode. Although a depressive episode is currently present, the psychotic symptoms are primary and independent, consistent with the diagnostic criteria for Schizophrenia.
